He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. Listed at {{convert|6|ft|11|in|m|2}},{{Cite web |title=James Wiseman {{!}} Player Profile |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1630164/james-wiseman |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20241108223542/https://www.nba.com/player/1630164/james-wiseman |archive-date=November 8, 2024 |access-date=November 8, 2024 |website=[[NBA.com]] |language=en-US}} he plays the [[center (basketball)|center]] position. Wiseman began high school at [[The Ensworth School]] in his hometown of [[Nashville, Tennessee]] before transferring to [[East High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Memphis East High School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], where he was coached by former NBA player [[Penny Hardaway]] for his first year. As a senior, Wiseman was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], with most recruiting services ranking him number one in the 2019 class. He claimed multiple national player of the year awards and played in the [[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]] after his final season. In college, Wiseman joined Memphis to play for Hardaway, who had become the Tigers' coach. Early into his freshman season, he was suspended by the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA), which deemed that Hardaway had acted as a [[Booster club|booster]] by facilitating Wiseman's move to [[Memphis, Tennessee]] in 2017. He served part of the suspension before withdrawing from school to prepare for the [[2020 NBA draft]], where he was drafted with the second overall pick by the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the team in [[2022 NBA Finals|2022]], despite being injured and not appearing in any games during the season. He was then traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in 2023, before signing with the [[Indiana Pacers]] in 2024. He is widely regarded as an NBA [[draft bust]].{{cite web | url=https://bluemanhoop.com/warriors-draft-bust-could-cut-this-week-after-devastating-injury | title=Warriors draft bust could be cut this week after devastating injury | date=January 7, 2025 }} ==High school career== Entering his freshman season for [[The Ensworth School]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee]], Wiseman stood {{height|ft=6|in=9}} and weighed {{Convert|200|lb}}. He was a teammate of future [[NBA]] player [[Jordan Bone]].{{cite web |last1=Bossi |first1=Eric |title=Wiseman, Bone impress in Nashville |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/wiseman-bone-impress-in-nashville |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=April 21, 2019 |date=December 5, 2015}} By June 2016, [[ESPN]] ranked Wiseman among its top 25 players in the 2020 recruiting class.{{cite web |title=17 EYBL players ranked in ESPN 2019 Top 25 |url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/657937-17-eybl-players-ranked-in-espn-2019-top-25 |publisher=D1Circuit |access-date=April 21, 2019 |date=June 9, 2016}} In 2016, he played for the St. Louis Eagles [[Amateur Athletic Union]] team.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Penny Hardaway, James Wiseman and the Memphis Tigers: A timeline |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28059747|publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 10, 2020 |date=December 19, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Medcalf |first2=Myron |last3=Merrill |first3=Liz |title=James Wiseman, Penny Hardaway and the high-stakes collision of two stars |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28340499|publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=April 10, 2020 |date=December 20, 2019}} As a sophomore in 2016–17, he guided Ensworth to the [[Tennessee Secondary School Athletic Association]] (TSSAA) Division II-AA semifinals.{{cite web |last1=McGaw |first1=Sam |title=Strong defense pushes BA basketball past Ensworth in state semifinal (basketball)|points]] and 10 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] per game and was named [[MaxPreps]] Sophomore All-American honorable mention.{{cite web |title=2016-17 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/MsrjHfTvwUaObsbpYQ-lYg/2016-17-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 21, 2019 |date=April 13, 2017}} In May 2017, Wiseman joined Team Penny, founded by former NBA player [[Penny Hardaway]], on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) circuit. In August, he announced his transfer to [[East High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Memphis East High School]] in [[Memphis, Tennessee]], where Hardaway was promoted to head coach.{{cite web |last1=Giannotto |first1=Mark |title=James Wiseman, a top 2019 basketball recruit, has transferred to Memphis East High School |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2017/08/21/james-wiseman-basketball-recruit-transfers-east-high-school-eligibility/586105001/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=August 21, 2017}} On November 16, 2017, the TSSAA ruled Wiseman ineligible for his junior season because an "athletic coaching link" existed between him and Hardaway.{{cite web |last1=Varlas |first1=John |title=Why Memphis East, a national power coached by Penny Hardaway, has 2 ineligible players |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/11/16/players-memphis-east-high-school-basketball-ruled-ineligible-penny-hardaway-james-wiseman-ryan-boyce/869116001/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=November 16, 2017}} However, on December 13, he was cleared to play because the TSSAA rule was "not clear in its application".{{cite web |last1=Ostrander |first1=Lynden |title=Memphis East basketball transfers Wiseman, Boyce ruled eligible |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/iqyytoW_MUCqoObAKGpGzg/memphis-east-basketball-transfers-wiseman,-boyce-ruled-eligible.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=December 13, 2017}} During the season, Wiseman rose to become the number one overall recruit by ESPN in the 2019 class. On March 17, 2018, he led Memphis East to a TSSAA Class AAA championship, leading all scorers with 19 points.{{cite web |last1=Varlas |first1=John |title=James Wiseman, the top player in Class of 2019, caps rough season with coveted title for East |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2018/03/17/james-wiseman-memphis-east-basketball-penny-hardaway-tssaa-state-tournament-whitehaven-tigers/435064002/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=March 17, 2018}} He averaged 18.5 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 2.8 [[block (basketball)|blocks]] per game, earning MaxPreps Junior All-American third team recognition.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2017-18 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/hNi1UD2amUag_PSRxexoDw/2017-18-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team-.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=April 13, 2018}} Entering his senior season, Wiseman remained at Memphis East instead of transferring to a [[College-preparatory school|prep school]], citing "the East High tradition" and the improvements he made as a |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/why-james-wiseman-stayed-at-memphis-east |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=March 16, 2019}} On March 1, 2019, he recorded a [[double (basketball)|triple-double]] of 27 points, 20 rebounds, and 10 blocks to help his team win the Region 8AAA championship.{{cite web |last1=Greer |first1=Jarvis |title=Wiseman leads East to region championship |url=http://www.wmcactionnews5.com/2019/03/01/wiseman-leads-east-region-championship/ |publisher=[[WMC-TV]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=March 1, 2019}} Memphis East finished 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Gallant |first1=Jacob |title=Wiseman wins Morgan Wootten Player of the Year |url=http://www.wmcactionnews5.com/2019/03/26/wiseman-wins-morgan-wootten-player-year/ |access-date=April 10, 2020 |date=November 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Wiseman was a consensus five-star recruit out of high school and was considered the top recruit in the 2019 class by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and [[ESPN]].{{cite web |title=James Wiseman, East, Center (BK) |url=https://247sports.com/Player/James-Wiseman-88248/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=April 22, 2019}}{{cite web |title=James Wiseman |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/224175/james-wiseman |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=October 31, 2020}} On November 20, 2018, he committed to [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] despite strongly considering [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]]. As a result, he reunited with former high school coach Penny Hardaway, who had become the team's head coach in the previous season.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=No. 1 recruit James Wiseman joining coach Penny Hardaway at Memphis |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25331935 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=October 31, 2020 |date=November 20, 2018}} On November 29, Wiseman signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play college basketball for Memphis.{{cite web |last1=Updahyay |first1=Sudu |title=James Wiseman officially signs with U of M |url=http://www.wmcactionnews5.com/2018/11/29/james-wiseman-officially-signs-with-u-m/ |publisher=[[WMC-TV]] |access-date=April 22, 2019 |date=November 29, 2018}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = James Wiseman | position = [[Center (basketball)|C]] | hometown = [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville, TN]] | highschool = [[East High School (Memphis, Tennessee)|Memphis East]] (TN) | feet = 7 | inches = 1 | weight = 230 | 40 = | commitdate = November 20, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 97 }} {{College athlete recruit end | 40 = | year = 2019 | rivals ref title = Memphis 2019 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2019 Memphis Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = memphis | scout s = | espn schoolid = 235 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 1 | 247 overall = 2 | espn overall = 1 | access-date = April 5, 2019 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Wiseman was projected to be the first overall pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. In August 2019, a minor shoulder injury kept Wiseman from joining Memphis for a series of preseason [[exhibition game]]s in [[Nassau, Bahamas]].{{cite web |last1=Munz |first1=Jason |title=Penny Hardaway updates James Wiseman's status, says Precious Achiuwa will not make trip to Bahamas |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/08/13/memphis-basketball-penny-hardaway-james-wiseman-commonwealth-bank-giants-precious-achiuwa-bahamas/1948853001/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=August 13, 2019}} He missed his team's two preseason games in October after sustaining an ankle injury.{{cite web |last1=Munz |first1=Jason |title=James Wiseman will not play vs. LeMoyne-Owen |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2019/10/28/memphis-basketball-james-wiseman-not-play-vs-lemoyne-owen/2488900001/ |website=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=October 28, 2019}} On November 5, Wiseman made his regular season debut with 28 points, 11 rebounds, and three blocks in 22 minutes as the Tigers defeated [[South Carolina State Bulldogs basketball|South Carolina State]], 97–64.{{cite news |title=Wiseman has 28 and 11 in winning debut for No. 14 Memphis |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401170001 |access-date=November 6, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} On November 8, Wiseman's lawyers announced that the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) ruled him ineligible to play for Memphis. The [[University of Memphis]] stated that head coach Penny Hardaway had paid for $11,500 in moving expenses to help him and his family move to the city of Memphis in 2017.{{cite magazine |last1=Pickman |first1=Ben |title=Memphis' James Wiseman Ruled Ineligible by NCAA, Will Play Friday After Court Order |url=https://www.si.com/college/2019/11/08/james-wiseman-memphis-ineligible-ncaa |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=November 8, 2019}} According to Wiseman's lawyer, Leslie Ballin, the NCAA deemed that Hardaway, a Memphis alumnus, had acted as a booster.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=NCAA rules Memphis' James Wiseman ineligible; top prospect gets stay to play Friday |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28037071|publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=November 8, 2019 |date=November 8, 2019}} On the same day, a [[Shelby County, Tennessee|Shelby County]] judge granted Wiseman a temporary [[restraining order]] against the NCAA's ruling, allowing him to keep playing.{{cite news|last=Walker|first=Teresa M.|title=Memphis, James Wiseman have 1 more game, then it's back to court|date=November 13, 2019|newspaper=The Spokesman-Review|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2019/nov/13/memphis-james-wiseman-have-1-more-game-then-its-ba/|access-date=November 14, 2019}} Less than two hours later, he had 17 points and nine rebounds to lead Memphis past [[UIC Flames men's basketball|UIC]], 92–46.{{cite news |title=Wiseman gets restraining order to play; Memphis wins |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169442 |access-date=December 11, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 8, 2019}} Wiseman's lawyers filed a lawsuit against the NCAA to restore his eligibility before withdrawing the case six days later in hopes of reaching an agreement.{{cite web |last1=Parrish |first1=Gary |title=Memphis' James Wiseman withdraws lawsuit against the NCAA, will sit in hopes of having eligibility restored |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/memphis-james-wiseman-withdraws-lawsuit-against-the-ncaa-will-sit-in-hopes-of-having-eligibility-restored/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=March 24, 2020 |date=November 14, 2019}} On November 20, the NCAA ruled that Wiseman would be eligible to return on January 12 after serving a 12-game suspension if he donated $11,500 to a charity of his choice.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2019/11/20/sports/ncaabasketball/james-wiseman-of-memphis-can-return-from-suspension-in-january.html|title=James Wiseman of Memphis Can Return From Suspension in January|last=Witz|first=Billy|date=November 20, 2019|work=The New York Times|access-date=November 22, 2019|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}} On December 19, 2019, after missing seven games due to suspension, Wiseman announced that he would leave Memphis, hire an [[sports agent|agent]] and prepare for the [[2020 NBA draft]], effectively ending his college career. He was one of the highest-rated prospects in his class, according to draft analysts.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28335497|title=James Wiseman leaves Memphis,
